knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes how marginals and conditionals are obtained from a joint distribution?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Marginals sum/integrate out partners; conditionals divide the joint by the conditioning event's probability. Skipping extraction or omitting normalisation confuses joint with margin or conditional.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Marginal: sum/integrate joint; conditional: joint divided by P(condition).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating the joint as sufficient without marginals/conditionals, or forgetting to divide by P(X = x).

choices.label: A marginal sums or integrates the joint over the other variable(s). A conditional renormalises the joint on the given condition, dividing by the marginal probability of that condition.
Marginal and conditional distributions are optional decorations once the joint table or density is written; the joint already contains all required information without extraction.
A conditional P(Y | X = x) equals the joint entry P(X = x, Y) with no division by P(X = x).
A marginal distribution is obtained by dividing each joint cell by the grand total of all cells; conditionals use the same rule.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.2.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Joint PMF of (X, Y): P(0,0)=0.10, P(0,1)=0.20, P(1,0)=0.30, P(1,1)=0.40. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute P(X=1) and P(Y=1 | X=1); refuse joint-as-margins-done.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Marginal sums the X = 1 row. Conditional divides 0.40 by 0.70. Using one cell as the marginal, skipping division, or wrong numerator are standard joint-table errors.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Largest-cell shortcut, conditional without normalising, or wrong numerator for P(Y=1|X=1).

choices.label: P(X=1) = 0.30 + 0.40 = 0.70. P(Y=1 | X=1) = 0.40 / 0.70 ≈ 0.571. The joint table is not interchangeable with its margins or conditionals without these moves.
P(X=1) = 0.40 because P(1,1) is the largest cell, so X = 1 is identified with that cell alone.
P(Y=1 | X=1) = 0.40 because the conditional equals the joint entry P(1,1) with no further normalisation.
P(X=1) = 0.70 and P(Y=1 | X=1) = 0.60 because (0.30 + 0.40) and (0.20 + 0.40) are both needed for the conditional numerator.

worked_example.title: Marginal and conditional from a joint claim table
worked_example.problem_statement: A policy year records indicators (X, Y) with joint PMF P(0,0) = 0.05, P(0,1) = 0.15, P(1,0) = 0.20, P(1,1) = 0.60, where X = 1 if a weather claim occurs and Y = 1 if a liability claim occurs. Compute P(X = 1) and P(Y = 0 | X = 1).
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Sum the X = 1 column for the marginal, then divide the joint cell by that marginal for the conditional.

steps.label: Form the marginal P(X = 1)
steps.attempt_cue: Add the joint probabilities with X = 1.
steps.explanation: The marginal for X = 1 sums over Y: P(X = 1) = P(1,0) + P(1,1).

steps.label: Form the conditional P(Y = 0 | X = 1)
steps.explanation: Conditional probability renormalises the joint cell by the matching marginal.

steps.label: Refuse joint-as-marginal
steps.attempt_cue: State why P(1,1) = 0.60 is not P(X = 1).
steps.explanation: A single joint cell is not a marginal. Marginals sum across the other variable; conditionals divide by that sum.

worked_example.final_answer: P(X = 1) = 0.80; P(Y = 0 | X = 1) = 0.25. The joint table is not interchangeable with its margins or conditionals without these moves.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Reporting P(X = 1) = 0.60 because P(1,1) is the largest cell, or taking P(Y = 0 | X = 1) = 0.20 without dividing by the marginal 0.80.
